characters.name: Hector Cruz
characters.description: One of the main characters of the series along with Ozzy and Drix. He is a 13-year-old boy whose body serves as the main setting for the series due to Ozzy and Drix being sucked out of FrankDeTorreby a mosquito and then ending up inside Hector, Audience Surrogate: Presumably the reason why the setting of the show was switched to the inside of his body as opposed to Frank's since he's a 13-year-old kid and the show is a Saturday morning kids cartoon. Big Eater: A recurring trait that is brought about him is that he eats a lot and will eat pretty much anything, to which Travislampshadesin "The Globfather" when Hector talks about a scary carnival ride.Hector: You'd have to be nuts to go on that. I'd rather eat my own foot.Travis: Eh, you'll eat anything. Born Unlucky: As his body is the main setting for the show, bad things happen to him a lot. From getting sick, to almost getting beaten up, and almost dying, Hector is lucky that Ozzy and Drix are always there to save him. Heroes Love Dogs: He really loves his dog, Uno. When they first met, Hector greatly worried that he’s gotten allergic to Uno, and his mother came really close to giving the latter away until they realized it was the pollen that made him sneeze a lot.

characters.name: Maria Amino
characters.description: Fair Cop: She's a very beautiful cell-cop. Ms. Fanservice: Slender, feisty, mature and wears a crop top that exposes her midriff. Makes one wonder if that's Hector's mom's genes shining through. Non-Mammal Mammaries: Amusingly, on a character who livesinsidea mammal. Spicy Latina: She has a very fiery personality. Statuesque Stunner: On a microscopic scale, mind you, but she's proportionally very tall.

characters.name: Ellen Patella
characters.description: Hello, Attorney!: Acts as one of the leading attorneys of Hector, and was the one who suggested that Ozzy and Drix opened their own freelance agency. Prim and Proper Bun: Her "hair" is shaped to resemble this.

characters.name: Mayor Spryman
characters.description: Bratty Half-Pint: Well, he is the inner embodiment of a teenager. A Child Shall Lead Them:Justified Trope. Hectorisa teenager after all. Fake Ultimate Hero: Constantly takes credit for Ozzy and Drix's captures of dangerous viruses. The opening sequence lampshades this. Hidden Heart of Gold: He trusts Ozzy and Drix to keep Hector healthy, in spite of butting heads with them frequently. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He can be a jerk sure, but he does mean well and cares a lot about Hector and the city.

characters.name: Chief Gluteus
characters.description: Da Chief: Downplayed. He always gives Osmosis a hard time, but he’s willing to listen to him and take his advice into account. Interspecies Romance: For averygenerous interpretation of species; he, an anthropomorphic muscle cell, has aShip Teasewith Drix's Auntie Histamine, an anthropomorphic chemical compound. Meaningful Name: Named for the Gluteus Maximus, which is the largest muscle in the human body. No-Sell: Being a muscle cell rather than a white blood cell, he's immune to things like allergens. Old Soldier: Well, Old Cop, but he gives off the impression of being far more experienced and older than the rest of the force.

characters.name: Backseat
characters.description: Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: To keep with the series’ biology theme, his mouth “wavelength” looks like a DNA molecule. Punny Name: Has the personality of a backseat driver. Silicon Snarker: Most of his lines are either sarcasm or whining about his chassis.Backseat(after Ozzy slips on grease and crashes into a lipid-bearing tanker): Nice work, speedy. At least you can skip the next oil change.

characters.name: Scarlet Fever
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: He’s utterly batshit insane, and the second he gets into Hector’s body he goes about trying to destroy everything in his path. Badass Decay:invokedIt’s implied that he used to be extremely powerful, but losing territory to the germs moving into Frank severely weakened him. Getting into Hector’s body allowed him to regain his badass. Cold Ham: He manages to devour the scenery without even raising his voice. Establishing Character Moment: He politely thanks a mechanic for building him a car customized specifically to his needs, and then tries to murder the mechanic after he asks to be payed for his work. Faux Affably Evil: Much like Thrax, he keeps up a polite facade that barely conceals the deranged monster within.

characters.name: Strepfinger
characters.description: Big Bad: The closest the show has to one as its most recurring villain. Whenever there's a plot going on in the background to release destructive plagues onto the city, he's often the mastermind. The show does continue after his final appearance, however. Evil Genius: He engineers plagues to unleash onto the city. Red Right Hand: His right hand's long clawed index finger, which is the basis of his name. Right-Hand Cat: He has a orange germ that fills this role. Shout-Out: His name is a combination of James Bond's two most infamous villains, Ernst Stavro Blofeld and Auric Goldfinger.

characters.name: Sylvian Fisher
characters.description: The Bad Guy Wins: Although he fails to become the new mayor of Hector, he successfully smashes Spryman afterHulking Out. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Maria mentions that he's a sweet guy. Think again. Card-Carrying Villain: His plans are literally labelled "evil plans". Evil Nerd: He's got the slouch, glasses, and nasally voice of a stereotypical nerd, and he's willing to harm Hector's body for political power. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: Wears glasses, and is willing to harm Hector in order to gain political power.

characters.name: The Pneumoniac
characters.description: Evil Laugh: As the Pneumoniac repeatedly announces his plans to infect Christine with pneumonia, he cackles evilly, which Maximusfinds annoying after a while.

characters.name: Chief Maximus
characters.description: Dirty Cop: Maximus is chief of the Christine PD, but is on Pneumoniac's payroll to help him unleash a pneumonia infection in Christine. The Smurfette Principle: Inverted and Deconstructed. He's seemingly the only competent male cop in Christine, but the rather extreme high and feminine standards of her body quickly drove him over the edge as per hisMotive Rant. This is what lead to him forming a deal with Pneumoniac to cause chaos within Christine, which will allow him to live his life freely in the theoretical mayhem.

characters.name: Cryo
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Personification: Cryo is unique in that she isn't a virus or bacteria but essentially a personification of hypothermia. This makes her one of the dangerous villains in the series. Near-Villain Victory: She cameveryclose to killing Hector, and if help hadn't found him in time, would have. Evenafterthat, Ozzy and Drix just barely manage to kill her. Person of Mass Destruction: Cryo is the embodiment of hypothermia, and basically a walking ice age. As such, she's one of the few threats Hector faces that isverycapable of killing Hector single-handedly.

characters.name: Nick O'Teen's Gang
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: Nick is nigh unbeatable so long as his host is addicted to him. The moment Hector breaks his addition, Nick is reduced to a powerless husk Ozzy easily kills. Anthropomorphic Vice: Nick and his gang represents cigarettes, its contents, and their effects. Notably, Nick actually is portrayed more as the personification of cigarette addiction rather thanjusta chemical. Brainwashed and Crazy: Nick O'Teen turns cells into his slaves with his powers, and intends to use Hector’s pleasure center to keep him hooked on cigarettes. Catchphrase: "I'm unbeatable!" for Nick O'Teen. Cruel and Unusual Death: Tar, Carbon Monoxide, and Butane are burnt alive by a nerve cell, while Nick O'Teen is stomped on by Ozzy.

characters.name: Lead Head Gang
characters.description: Brought to You by the Letter "S": Their leader has "PB" (the chemical symbol for lead; also his name) on his chest; the others just have "L". Leitmotif: They are usually accompanied by heavy electric guitar wailing. No-Sell: Due to being inorganic metals, they resist just about everything that Ozzy and Drix can throw at them. Outside-Context Problem: Rather than the show's usual germ foes, they're toxicmetals. Pun-Based Creature: Literal living lead with the personalities of the worst kind of heavy metal fan.

characters.name: The Supplements
characters.description: Action Girl: Vitamin E, the only female member, isn't any less of an asskicker than the rest. Broken Pedestal:Downplayed, but after spending the entire episode completely fanboying over them, Drix is disappointed when they prove incapable of doing anything when the Lead Heads take Mayor Spryman hostage. Brought to You by the Letter "S": All except for Iron have their vitamin letter somewhere on their body. Cyclops: For some reason, Vitamin D has only one giant eye. A Dog Named "Dog": Their names are all what chemical they are.
